claims.text: First: Doppler and color Doppler measures blood flow from the frequency shift of sound reflected by moving red blood cells
claims.quote: Doppler ultrasound is used to assess blood flow. It uses the Doppler effect (alteration of sound frequency by reflection off a moving object). The moving objects are red blood cells in blood.

claims.text: Color: the shade shows direction (for example red toward the probe, blue away); brightness shows average speed
claims.quote: Direction of blood flow is indicated by the shade of color (eg, red for blood flow toward the transducer, blue for blood flow away from the transducer). Average blood flow velocity is indicated by the brightness of the color

claims.text: Doppler is used to find occlusion and narrowing (stenosis) of vessels
claims.quote: To detect occlusion and stenosis of blood vessels

claims.text: Veins: looking for DVT DVT is usually diagnosed by duplex ultrasound (ultrasound with Doppler flow studies)
claims.quote: Diagnosis is typically by ultrasound with Doppler flow studies (duplex ultrasound).

claims.text: Signs of clot: the clot seen in the vein, a vein that does not compress normally, or impaired flow on Doppler
claims.quote: Ultrasound identifies thrombi by directly visualizing the venous lining and by demonstrating abnormal vein compressibility or, with Doppler flow studies, impaired venous flow.

claims.text: On color Doppler, a clot shows as a filling defect in the flow
claims.quote: The image on the right shows a filling defect on color Doppler flow. These findings are consistent with thrombus.
claims.locator: Doppler Ultrasound of a Patient with a Thrombus in Femoral Vein (image caption)

claims.text: About 90% sensitive and 98% specific for lower extremity DVT
claims.quote: The test is approximately 90% sensitive and 98% specific for lower extremity DVT
